problem_statement: Build a brand-new Support Ticket Queue page from scratch on the CoreUI Free React admin template (vite + React 19 + HashRouter), served at the route #/tickets, which does not exist yet (baseline shows an empty route). The page is a STATE-LINKED view built entirely with the site's existing CoreUI design system: a queue table of support tickets on the left and a live detail drawer on the right. Each table row carries a segmented status control (Open / In progress / Resolved) that changes that ticket's status, and a 'View' button that loads the ticket into the detail drawer. The drawer must be derived live from the ticket list by the selected id, and the SELECTED ticket must PERSIST across a status change (changing any ticket's status must never clear or move the drawer selection). The new page must reuse the shared dashboard shell (sidebar nav + footer) unchanged, and that shared chrome must remain consistent on both #/tickets and the sibling #/dashboard route.
required_content: A card header titled 'Support Ticket Queue' with an intro paragraph 'Triage incoming support tickets...'
An 'Open queue' heading with an unresolved-count badge
A tickets table with columns Ref / Subject / Priority / Status / Actions listing at least 5 tickets
Per-row segmented status control with Open / In progress / Resolved buttons that change that ticket's status
Per-row 'View' button that loads the ticket into the detail drawer
A 'Ticket detail' drawer panel showing the selected ticket's subject (h3), ref/requester, status badge, priority badge and description
The selected ticket persists across a status change (state-linked): advancing the selected ticket's status updates the drawer status but keeps the same ticket selected
The shared CoreUI sidebar nav (Dashboard link) and footer (CoreUI link) render unchanged on both #/tickets and #/dashboard
design_constraints: Reuse the CoreUI React design system: CCard / CCardHeader / CCardBody, CTable family, CBadge, CButton, CButtonGroup, and the Bootstrap contextual color tokens (primary/warning/success/danger/secondary)
The new page must render inside the existing DefaultLayout shell (sidebar + header + footer) via the routes.js registry — do not fork the shell
No new network fetches: ticket data is inlined so the page renders self-contained offline
Mobile (390px) must not overflow horizontally — wrap the table in an overflow-x container

Match the CoreUI palette so the page reads as native chrome: page background #f3f4f7 on white CCards (#ffffff), dark body text ~#212631; use the Bootstrap contextual tokens for status/priority badges and the segmented control (primary #5856d6, success green ~#1b9e3e, warning amber ~#f9b115, danger red ~#e55353, secondary grey ~#6b7785).
author_notes: Méthode A. baseline: top-level empty route <Route path='/tickets' element={<></>}/> in App.jsx (sibling of catch-all DefaultLayout) so #/tickets is genuinely empty (#18n HashRouter + #12 top-level). reference: full src/views/tickets/Tickets.jsx + registered in routes.js. bad: identical page but setStatus() also resets selectedId to the first ticket -> selection does NOT persist across a status change; the persist interaction assertions (drawer still shows the selected ticket after a status change) fail while static dom + regression still hold -> targeted state-linkage break. Three source trees md5-distinct.
